QASHANI:11:41-43/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:41-43/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:41-43/r1.claim: God's greatest Name is the existence of a complete human knower, prophet, imam, or scholar through whom a law is carried into and established in the corporeal world.
QASHANI:11:41-43/r1.anchor: باسم الله الأعظم الذي هو وجود كل عارف كامل من أفراد نوع الإنسان

QASHANI:11:41-43/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:41-43/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:41-43/r2.claim: God forgives dark bodily dispositions and nature's sins through adherence to law and shows mercy by pouring out knowledge, unveiling, and luminous traits that save from drowning.
QASHANI:11:41-43/r2.anchor: يغفر هيئات نفوسكم البدنية المظلمة وذنوب ملابس الطبيعة المهلكة إياكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r1.claim: The preposition في is emphatic, and بسم الله may be a circumstantial phrase or indicate seeking blessing in God's name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r1.anchor: والباء في بسم الله في موضع الحال، أو متبركين بسم الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r2.claim: مجراها and مرساها may be accusative time or place adverbs, or verbal nouns with an omitted genitive such as the time of arrival; their governing force comes from the action implied by باسم الله.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r2.anchor: ومجراها ومرساها منصوبان إما على أنهما ظرفا زمان أو مكان، لأنهما يجيئان لذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r3.claim: Alternatively, باسم الله is circumstantial to فيها, while مجراها and مرساها are nominative subjects as verbal nouns; another parse makes them a coordinated subject with باسم الله as predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون باسم الله حالا من ضمير فيها، ومجراها ومرساها مصدران مرفوعان على الفاعلية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r4.claim: On the proposed subject or predicate parses, the sentence cannot be a circumstantial clause of اركبوا because it lacks a returning pronoun; it may instead be a second, independent sentence after the boarding command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز مع رفع مجراها ومرساها على الفاعلية أو الابتداء أن يكون حالا من ضمير اركبوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r5.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says Noah pronounced the formula to start the ship, and repeated it to make the ship stop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: إذا أراد جري السفينة قال بسم الله مجراها فتجري، وإذا أراد وقوفها قال بسم الله مرساها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r6.claim: Most named readers use مجراها with a ḍamma, while the two Hamza-family readers and Ḥafṣ use fatḥa; all keep a ḍamma in مرساها, and Ibn Masud and others open both vowels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد، والحسن، وأبو رجاء، والأعرج، وشيبة، والجمهور من السبعة الحرميان، والعربيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r7.claim: Several readers use the active participles مجريها and مرسيها; Abu Hayyan parses them as predicate substitutes for God's name, rejecting Ibn Atiyya's adjective parse unless the forms are made definite by non-pure annexation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r7.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك، والنخعي، وابن وثاب، وأبو رجاء، ومجاهد، وابن جندب، والكلبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r8.claim: غفور means God covers the believers' sins through repentance and faith, and رحيم describes His mercy in rescuing them from drowning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p155/r8.anchor: إن ربي لغفور ستور عليكم ذنوبكم بتوبتكم وإيمانكم، رحيم لكم إذا نجاكم من الغرق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p156/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p156/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p156/r1.claim: A report says Noah boarded on the first day of Rajab and fasted the whole month; Ikrima instead dates boarding to ten days into Rajab.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p156/r1.anchor: إن نوحا ركب في السفينة أول يوم من رجب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs read مجريها with an opened meem and its verbal sense of running, while the accompanying مَرساها has a damma.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص: "مجريها" بفتح الميم أي: جريها "ومرساها"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r2.speaker: محمد بن محيصن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r2.claim: Ibn Muhaysin opens both initial meem vowels and derives the verbal nouns from the verbs “ran” and “came to rest.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r2.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن محيصن "مجريها ومرساها بفتح الميمين من جرت ورست،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r3.claim: The remaining readers use the damma forms for the causative verbs “to set running” and “to moor”; these are verbal nouns, like the cited forms in 23:29 and 17:80.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r3.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: "مجراها ومرساها" بضم الميمين من أجريت وأرسيت، أي: بسم الله إجراؤها وإرساؤها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r4.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says Noah said “In God’s name” whenever he wanted the ark to sail or to come to rest.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r4.anchor: قال الضحاك: كان نوح إذا أراد أن تجري السفينة قال: بسم الله، فجرت، وإذا أراد أن ترسو قال: بسم الله، فرست.

DURR-FULL:v4p432/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r1.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says Noah spoke the basmala when he wanted the Ark to stop, and it stopped; when he wanted it to move, it moved.
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: كان إذا أراد أن ترسي قال: بسم الله فأرست وإذا أراد أن تجري قال: بسم الله فجرت

DURR-FULL:v4p432/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud recited the phrase with the wording “its sailing and its anchoring.”
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه كان يقرأ {مجراها ومرساها}

DURR-FULL:v4p432/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r3.claim: A report from Husayn ibn Ali says a person boarding a ship is protected from drowning by saying the basmala, the Ark verse, and “they did not measure God rightly.”
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r3.anchor: عن الحسين بن علي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمان لأمتي من الغرق إذا ركبوا في السفن

DURR-FULL:v4p432/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas similarly gives the basmala and the phrase about God's measure as protection from drowning at sea.
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أمان لأمتي من الغرق إذا ركبوا في السفن

DURR-FULL:v4p432/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises safety from drowning until leaving the ship to anyone who recites the prescribed formulas when boarding.
DURR-FULL:v4p432/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما رفعه ما من رجل يقول إذا ركب السفينة: بسم الله الملك الرحمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r1.claim: Readers vocalizing both mims with ḍamma understand the ship's running and anchoring as by God; readers with fatḥa understand God as the agent of their occurrence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r1.anchor: ومن قرأ بضم الميمين فالمعنى بالله إجراؤها وبالله إرساها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r2.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r2.claim: Abu Mansur distinguishes the readings as causative, “God made it run,” versus intransitive, “it ran.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r2.anchor: وسمعت شيخنا أبا منصور اللغوي يقول من ضم الميم في مجراها أراد أجراها الله مجرى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that Noah said “In God's name” when he wanted the ark to sail and again when he wanted it to anchor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك كان إذا أراد أن تجري قال بسم الله فجرت وإذا أراد أن ترسى قال بسم الله فرست

JISHUMI:v5p3499/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r2.claim: They read مجراها with fatḥa on mīm; the others read with ḍamma.
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص عن عاصم: مجراها بفتح الميم، والباقون بضم الميم

JISHUMI:v5p3499/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r3.speaker: محمد بن محيصن
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r3.claim: All readers except Muḥammad ibn Muḥayṣin use ḍamma in مرساها; he opens both mīms and treats both words as verbal nouns meaning the Ark's running and anchoring by God.
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r3.anchor: واتفقوا على ضم [ميم] مرساها غير محمد بن محيصن، فإنه فتح الميمين

JISHUMI:v5p3499/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r4.claim: With ḍamma, the words mean God causes the Ark to run and anchor, like Qur'anic verbal-noun forms for lodging, entering, and exiting; matching the two vowels is preferred.
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r4.anchor: فأما ضم الميمين فمعناه بالله إجراؤها وإرساؤها، كقوله: (أنزلني منزلا مباركا)

JISHUMI:v5p3499/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r5.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r5.claim: Ḥafṣ reads يابني with fatḥa on yāʾ throughout the Qur'an; the other readers use kasra, except for Ibn Kathīr's differing report in Luqmān.
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r5.anchor: وقرأ حفص عن عاصم: يابني بفتح الياء في جميع القرآن، والباقون جميع ذلك بالكسر

JISHUMI:v5p3499/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r6.claim: The kasra reading transfers the vowel of the deleted hamzat al-waṣl to yāʾ; fatḥa is lighter, while yāʾ and kasra together are considered heavy.
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r6.anchor: وأما الكسر فإنها لما حذفت ألف الوصل نقلت حركته إلى الياء، وأما الفتح فلأنه أخف الحركات

JISHUMI:v5p3499/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r7.claim: Jary means rapid movement and can name an agent or trustee because he acts in place of his principal.
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r7.anchor: الجري: مر سريع، وهو مصدر جرى جريا وجريه وجريانا، ويسمى الوكيل جريا

JISHUMI:v5p3499/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r8.claim: Irsa is securing a ship so that it stops; related usages describe something fixed or standing firm, including mountains and cooking pots.
JISHUMI:v5p3499/r8.anchor: والإرساء: إمساك السفينة بما تقف به، أرساها إرساء، ورست رسوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r1.claim: ‘By the name of God’ means that the ship's movement and docking occur by His power and command.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r2.claim: One reading has مجراها and مرساها with an open mīm, analyzed as verbal nouns, times, or places.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r3.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r3.claim: Mujahid read مجريها مرسيها as active participles in the genitive, describing God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r3.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد { * مجريها ومرسيها } بلفظ اسم الفاعل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r4.claim: The phrase may be an inserted sentence: Noah tells them to board, then says the ship's course and anchoring are by God's name, command, and power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r4.anchor: معناه أن نوحا عليه السلام أمرهم بالركوب ، ثم أخبرهم بأن مجراها ومرساها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r5.claim: Alternatively, it is a circumstantial phrase modifying the ship, meaning it was made to sail and anchor by God's name; compare the command to enter Paradise eternally.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون غير مقتضيه بأن تكون في موضع الحال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r6.claim: God's forgiveness and mercy are why He saved Noah's people; without them they would not have been rescued.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p374/r6.anchor: لولا مغفرته لذنوبكم ورحمته إياكم لما نجاكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r1.claim: Qatada says Noah boarded the ark on 10 Rajab and left it on 10 Muharram, Ashura; he told those fasting to complete the fast and the others to fast that day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r1.anchor: قال قتادة : ركب نوح عليه السلام في السفينة في اليوم العاشر من رجب , ونزل منها في اليوم العاشر من المحرم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r2.claim: Mujrayaha means setting the vessel in motion and mursaha means bringing it to rest; Noah said God's name when starting and stopping it.

MUQATIL:11:41-43/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:41-43/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:41-43/r1.claim: Noah tells the passengers to say God's name when the ark starts and stops; God is forgiving and merciful for saving them from punishment.
MUQATIL:11:41-43/r1.anchor: { وقال اركبوا فيها } في السفينة { بسم الله } إذا ركبتموها، فقولوا: بسم الله { مجراها } حين تجري،

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r1.claim: Mujahid says the other mountains rose above the flood, whose water stood fifteen cubits over them, while al-Judi lowered itself and the Ark rested there.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تشامخت الجبال وتطاولت لئلا ينالها الغرق فعلا الماء فوقها خمسة عشر ذراعا، وتطامن

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r9.claim: Ibn Asakir transmits from al-Hasan that Noah was the first messenger sent to earth and preached for 950 years amid widespread sin and tyranny.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r9.anchor: ذكر الحافظ ابن عساكر في التاريخ له عن الحسن: أن نوحا أول رسول بعثه الله

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r10.claim: Noah preached day and night, openly and secretly, with patience; people beat and expelled him, yet he prayed for their forgiveness rather than against them.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44/r10.anchor: وكان نوح يدعوهم ليلا ونهارا، سرا وعلانية، وكان صبورا حليما، ولم يلق أحد من الأنبياء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد وعبيد بن عمير
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r1.claim: They say Noah's people beat him until he fainted; on waking he prayed, Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r1.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعبيد بن عمير: كانوا يضربونه حتى يغشى عليه فإذا أفاق قال: «رب اغفر

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Noah was beaten, wrapped in felt and left for dead, then returned to preach; a boy later struck and wounded him with his father's staff.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن نوحا كان يضرب ثم يلف في لبد فيلقى في بيته يرون

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r3.claim: After Noah prayed for either the people's guidance or patience until judgment, God told him no more believers would come from them and ordered him not to grieve.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r3.anchor: فأوحى الله إليه وآيسه من إيمان قومه، وأخبره أنه لم يبق في أصلاب الرجال ولا

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas places Noah's home in Damascus and says he built the Ark from Lebanese wood between Zamzam and the Black Stone and Station.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانت دار نوح عليه السلام دمشق، وأنشأ سفينته من خشب لبنان بين

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r7.claim: The Ark's lower deck carried beasts, the next wild animals and birds, and the upper deck forty men and forty women, with ants kept above so larger animals would not trample them.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r7.anchor: فلما كملت حمل فيها السباع والدواب في الباب الأول، وجعل الوحش والطير في الباب الثاني

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r8.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r8.claim: Al-Zuhri says God sent a wind that carried pairs of every beast, bird, and livestock animal to Noah.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r8.anchor: قال الزهري: إن الله عز وجل بعث ريحا فحمل إليه من كل زوجين اثنين من

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r9.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r9.claim: Jaafar ibn Muhammad says Gabriel gathered the animals, placing his right hand on the male and left on the female, then putting them aboard.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r9.anchor: وقال جعفر بن محمد: بعث الله جبريل فحشرهم، فجعل يضرب بيديه على الزوجين فتقع يده

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r10.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r10.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit explains the goat's crooked tail and exposed sex as punishment for resisting Noah, while Noah's touch covered the ewe's sex.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r10.anchor: وقال زيد بن ثابت: استصعبت على نوح الماعزة أن تدخل السفينة، فدفعها بيده في ذنبها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r11.speaker: رجل من أهل العلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r11.claim: An unnamed scholar told Ishaq that a female hoopoe died aboard before land appeared; its mate buried her in its nape, explaining the tuft on hoopoes' necks.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#2/r11.anchor: قال إسحق: أخبرنا رجل من أهل العلم أن نوحا حمل أهل السفينة، وجعل فيها من

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says Noah carried every kind of tree in the Ark, including a date palm from Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r1.anchor:
وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" كان حمل نوح معه في السفينة من جميع

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r2.speaker: صاحب كتاب العروس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r2.claim: A story says Noah first sent a crow to report on the land; it found a carcass and stayed, so Noah cursed it to be killed anywhere and to fear people and homes.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r2.anchor: وذكر صاحب كتاب «العروس» وغيره: أن نوحا عليه السلام لما أراد أن يبعث من يأتيه

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r3.speaker: صاحب كتاب العروس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r3.claim: In the same story, the dove returned with an olive leaf, then later with red mud from the valley of the Sanctuary; Noah granted its requests for a neck ring, red feet, and residence there, and blessed its descendants.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r3.anchor: وبعث الحمامة فلم تجد قرارا فوقعت على شجرة بأرض سيناء فحملت ورقة زيتونة، ورجعت إلى

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r4.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r4.claim: Al-Tha'labi says Noah sent a partridge after the crow; it found greenery and stayed away, so Noah kept its offspring as hostages until Judgment Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-44#3/r4.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي أنه بعث بعد الغراب التدرج وكان من جنس الدجاج وقال: إياك أن تعتذر

RAZI-FULL:v17p184/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p184/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p184/r1.claim: Rāzī asks why Noah invoked forgiveness and mercy amid destruction; he answers that the survivors might credit their own knowledge for safety, so God reminded them that everyone needs divine grace and pardon.
RAZI-FULL:v17p184/r1.anchor: وأما قوله : { إن ربى لغفور رحيم } ففيه سؤال وهو أن ذلك الوقت وقت الإهلاك

TABRISI:11:40-43/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:40-43/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:40-43/r1.claim: The explanation of the reading فتح مجريها appeals to the following phrase وهي تجري بهم; the kasra reading is supported by the equivalent senses of جرت بهم and أجرتهم.
TABRISI:11:40-43/r1.anchor: وحجة من فتح مجريها قوله وهي تجري بهم ولو كان مجراها لكان وهي تجريهم

TABRISI:11:40-43/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:40-43/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:40-43/r2.claim: The verbs جرى and أجرى are close in meaning, whether one says a thing sailed, made it sail, or sailed with it.
TABRISI:11:40-43/r2.anchor: يقال: جرى الشيء وأجريته وجريت به

TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r13.claim: The passengers are told to board the ark, with omitted narrative understood: after the flood began and Noah recognized God's sign of the unbelievers' destruction, he called his family and followers aboard.
TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r13.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره فلما فار التنور ووقف نوح على ما دله الله عليه

TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r14.claim: They invoke God's name for blessing at the ark's setting out and anchoring.
TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r14.anchor: متبركين باسم الله أو قائلين بسم الله وقت إجرائها ووقت إرساؤها

TABRISI:11:43#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:43#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:11:43#2/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says they said God's name when they wanted the ark to sail, and again when they wanted it to stop.
TABRISI:11:43#2/r1.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كانوا إذا أرادوا أن تجري السفينة

TABRISI:11:43#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:43#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:43#2/r2.claim: Mentioning God as forgiving and merciful follows the account of rescue by boarding: mercy is sought through obedience just as rescue came through boarding.
TABRISI:11:43#2/r2.anchor: لما ذكرت النجاة بالركوب في السفينة ذكرت النعمة بالمغفرة والرحمة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r1.claim: Noah told those aboard to board the ark, invoking God's name for sailing and landing; saying the name made the ship move or stop.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r1.anchor: يريد: تجري باسم الله، وترسي باسم الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r2.claim: Noah described God as forgiving and merciful to those aboard.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Believers should trust God and His mercy, not the Ark or other material means, however important those means are.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: believers in reality should trust God and His mercy and not these resources.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God provides the means people rely on, and they work only at His behest; beginning activities with the blessed words reminds believers to look beyond appearances.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: these means and resources work at His behest

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: People should not rely wholly on means or on their own pious deeds; their real trust belongs in God's mercy and forgiveness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the real trust should actually be on the mercy and forgiveness of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: A person cannot know what weight any particular deed will carry in God's scale.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Who knows which deed occupies what weight in His scale

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.claim: مقام can name the action or place of إقامة; مجراها and مرساها are likewise parsed as verbal nouns.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p204#2/r3.anchor: وأما أقام يقيم فالمصدر والموضع يجيئان منه على مقام،

ELMALILI:11:40-42/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:40-42/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:40-42/r23.claim: On this syntax, the oven’s boiling marks the completion of the ship’s construction and the start of loading and movement; the ship’s engine is firing up.
ELMALILI:11:40-42/r23.anchor: nihâyet emrimiz gelip gemi fayrab edildiği vakit

ELMALILI:11:40-42/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:40-42/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:40-42/r25.claim: The objection that such a steamship could not have been made then, or that its craft would not have been forgotten, is only incredulity.
ELMALILI:11:40-42/r25.anchor: o zaman öyle bir vapur nasıl yapılabilirdi ve yapılmış olsa bu sanat unutulur mu idi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:41/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:41/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:41/r1.claim: Noah tells them to board the ark and invoke God’s name while it sails and comes to rest, affirming that his Lord is forgiving and merciful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:41/r1.anchor: Yüzerken de dururken de Allah’ın adını anın

BURSEVI:v4p79/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r1.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p79/r1.claim: Al-Kawashi parses “in God’s name is its running and mooring” with “running” as the subject, “in God’s name” as its predicate, and “mooring” coordinated; Noah invoked God at both launch and landing.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r1.anchor: بسم الله مجراها خبر ومبتدأ ومرساها عطف عليه

BURSEVI:v4p79/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r2.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p79/r2.claim: The reading of majrāhā with either a or u is a verbal noun from two synonymous forms, while marsāhā with u derives from the ship coming to rest.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r2.anchor: ومجراها ضما وفتحا مصدر أجريته وجريت به لغتان بمعنى

BURSEVI:v4p79/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p79/r3.claim: God’s forgiveness of sins and mercy toward servants explain their rescue from this catastrophe.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r3.anchor: إن ربي لغفور للذنوب والخطايا رحيم لعباده ولهذا نجاكم من هذه الداهية

BURSEVI:v4p79/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p79/r4.claim: Their rescue was not earned by merit but came solely through God’s favor, forgiveness, and mercy, as Sunni doctrine maintains.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r4.anchor: نجاتهم ليست بسبب استحقاقهم لها بل بمحض فضل الله وغفرانه ورحمته

BURSEVI:v4p79/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p79/r5.claim: A believing old woman asked Noah to tell her when to board, but he forgot while loading the ark; she later found that God had saved her safely inside her house without her seeing the flood.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r5.anchor: قد وقع وكان أمر الله مفعولا وتعجب من أمر العجوز فإن الله تعالى قد أنجاها في بيتها

BURSEVI:v4p79/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r6.speaker: بعض أهل الكشف
BURSEVI:v4p79/r6.claim: Some people of spiritual unveiling identify the site of Bursa’s Great Mosque as the old woman’s house.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r6.anchor: قد صح عن بعض أهل الكشف أن موضع الجامع الكبير في بلدة بروسه كان بيتا للعجوز المذكورة

BURSEVI:v4p79/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r7.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v4p79/r7.claim: The Mathnawi says perfected people can know and see a person from afar, even years before birth, in proportion to the polish of their inner perception.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r7.anchor: كاملان ازدور نامت بشنوند تا بقعرباد وبودت درروند

BURSEVI:v4p79/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p79/r8.claim: The Sharia’s ark saves from the tempests of the lower self and world; merely boarding by instinct or imitation, as hypocrites and Iblis did, gives no true rescue, which requires obeying the divine command.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r8.anchor: من ركب سفينة الشرع بالطبع وتقليد الآباء والاستاذين لم ينفعه للنجاة الحقيقية

BURSEVI:v4p79/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p79/r9.claim: “In God’s name” means the ark’s movement originates from God and its return is to God, as the verse says the final destination is to the Lord.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r9.anchor: يكون مجريها من الله ومرساها إلى الله كقوله : إن إلى ربك المنتهى

BURSEVI:v4p79/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p79/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p79/r10.claim: In the ishari reading, God is forgiving to those saved by boarding the ark and merciful to those who board by command rather than instinct.
BURSEVI:v4p79/r10.anchor: بالنجاة لمن ركبها رحيم لمن ركبها بالأمر لا بالطبع

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r1.claim: These readers pronounce the mīm of majrāhā with ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر: مجراها بضم الميم.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r2.claim: These readers pronounce the mīm with fatḥa and the rāʾ with kasra; the source notes this is the Qurʾan’s only rāʾ with kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: مجراها بفتح الميم وكسر الراء، وكذلك حفص عن عاصم

QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#1/r1.claim: The reading applies imāla to the alif, tilting fatḥa toward kasra on rāʾ as a dialectal phonetic feature.
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#1/r1.anchor: Imāla of the alif — tilting fatḥa toward kasra on the rāʾ, dialectal phonetic feature

QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#2/r1.claim: The Form IV active participle presents God as the agent who makes the ark flow, rather than naming its course.
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#2/r1.anchor: God as agent causing the ark's motion, not the course itself

QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#3/r1.claim: The imāla variant keeps the active, divinely caused sense while tilting the vowel dialectally.
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#3/r1.anchor: same semantic shift to divine agency plus dialectal vowel tilting

QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#4/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#4/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#4/r1.claim: The maṣdar or place noun conveys the ark's being made to flow, with a passive sense of divine causation.
QIRAAT-ER:11:41:8#4/r1.anchor: passive sense: the ark's divinely-caused flowing

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r1.claim: رسا الشيء means that a thing became fixed and settled; a cited line depicts a free soul remaining firm as a coward's soul rises.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r1.anchor: رسا الشيء يرسو، ثبت واستقر. قال: فصبرت نفسا عند ذلك حرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r2.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ report both kasra and fatḥa on the lām in بلع; البالوعة is a place that absorbs water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r2.anchor: والفعل منه بلع بكسر اللام وبفتحها لغتان حكاهما الكسائي والفراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r3.claim: إقلاع means stopping; it is said of rain and fever, and more generally of leaving something, a sense close to ceasing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r3.anchor: الإقلاع: الإمساك، يقال: أقلع المطر، وأقلعت الحمى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r4.claim: غاض الماء means the water diminished, while غاضته means someone diminished it; the verb is both intransitive and transitive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r4.anchor: غاض الماء نقص في نفسه، وغضته نقصته، جاء لازما ومتعديا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r12.claim: The pronoun in وقال refers to Noah, speaking to the believers and those he was ordered to carry; taking God as speaker is unlikely because Noah says إن ربي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r12.anchor: الضمير في: وقال، عائد على نوح أي: وقال نوح حين أمر بالحمل في السفينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r13.claim: Another view makes God the speaker addressing Noah and his companions, but Abū Ḥayyān finds it unlikely given إن ربي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r13.anchor: وقيل: الضمير عائد على الله، والتقدير: وقال الله لنوح ومن معه، ويبعد ذلك قوله: إن ربي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r14.claim: Although some say the rational beings dominate the plural address despite being few, he takes اركبوا as addressed specifically to humans because it does not fit irrational creatures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r14.anchor: قيل: وغلب من يعقل في قوله: اركبوا، وإن كانوا قليلا بالنسبة لما لا يعقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r15.claim: اركبوا takes في because it includes the sense of move into it or enter it; another analysis supplies الماء as its object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r15.anchor: وعدي اركبوا بفي لتضمينه معنى صيروا فيها، أو معنى ادخلوا فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r16.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p154/r16.claim: Another syntactic explanation supplies الماء: ride the water while in the ship.

QUSHAYRI:v2p44/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p44/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p44/r9.claim: Noah's safety in the flood came through God's name, reliance upon Him, and His favor, not through multiplying schemes.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r1.claim: Noah is the speaker addressing the believers with him; the phrase about his Lord's forgiveness signals this attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r1.anchor: أي نوح عليه السلام لمن معه من المؤمنين كما ينبيء عنه قوله تعالى : ( إن ربي لغفور رحيم )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r2.claim: A view makes God the speaker, but al-Alusi objects that the wording would then naturally be my Lord, not your Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : الضمير لله تعالى وفيه أنه لو كان كذلك لكان المناسب إن ربكم إلخ

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r3.claim: He suggests Noah said this after loading the pairs that he had been commanded to carry into the Ark.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r3.anchor: ولعل هذا القول بعد إدخال ما أمر بحمله في الفلك من الأزواج

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r4.claim: Here ride means enter or settle in the Ark; calling it riding compares the vessel on water to a mount on land, a derived metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r4.anchor: أي صيروا فيها وجعل ذلك ركوبا لأنها في الماء كالمركوب في الأرض ففيه استعارة تبعية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r5.speaker: القاضي البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r5.claim: Al-Baydawi treats the expression as an implicit metaphor, with the preposition marking the transition into the vessel.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : استعارة مكنية والتعدية بفي لاعتبار الصيرورة وإلا فالفعل يتعدى بنفسه وإلى هذا ذهب القاضي البيضاوي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r6.claim: Another explanation says the preposition fi is used because the verb includes the sense of entering.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r6.anchor: وقيل : التعدية بذلك لأنه ضمن معنى إدخلوا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r7.claim: Another explanation supplies water as the object: ride the water in the Ark.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r8.claim: A further view treats fi as an emphatic extra preposition.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r9.claim: Al-Alusi says the first explanation of the preposition is the most apt.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r10.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r10.claim: A riding verb applied to a moving object takes fi to preserve its locative sense; this does not mean the passengers were inside, since reports place them above.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r10.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين : الركوب العلو على شيء متحرك ويتعدى بنفسه وإستعماله بفي ليس لأن المأمور به كونهم في جوفها لا فوقها كما ظن

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r11.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r11.claim: Riding means mounting something moving, voluntarily like an animal or by force like a ship; the verb is direct with animals but takes fi with ships.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r11.anchor: معنى الركوب العلو على شيء له حركة إما إرادية كالحيوان أو قسرية كالسفينة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r12.claim: The apparent reading is literal riding here, although some explicitly say the usage is not literal.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p55#3/r12.anchor: وظاهره أن الركوب ههنا حقيقي وصرح بعضهم أنه ليس به

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r1.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r1.claim: Al-Raghib says riding originally means being on an animal's back, though it is also used for ships.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r1.anchor: وقال الراغب : الركوب في الأصل كون الإنسان على ظهر حيوان وقد يستعمل في السفينة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r2.claim: Bismi llah is a circumstantial phrase attached to the subject of ride; its bāʾ marks accompaniment, meaning they ride while naming God.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r2.anchor: ولما كانت ملابسة إسم الله عز إسمه بذكره قالوا : المعنى إركبوا مسمين الله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r3.claim: Alternatively, an omitted circumstantial phrase is supplied: ride while saying bismi llah, with the quoted phrase standing in its place.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r3.anchor: وجوزوا أن تكون الحال محذوفة وهذا معمول لها ساد مسدها ولذلك سموه حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r4.claim: Majraha and mursaha may be temporal accusatives, as verbal nouns or time-nouns, with an omitted waqt understood as in the example about the star's setting.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r4.anchor: نصب على الظرفية أي وقت إجرائها وإرسائها على أنهما إسما زمان أو مصدران ميميان

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r5.claim: They may instead be place-nouns governed by the locative phrase or by saying; they cannot sensibly be governed by ride, whose command is to seek blessing or say God's name there.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونا غسمي مكان وإنتصابهما بالإستقرار الذي تعلق به الجار والمجرور أو بقائلين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r6.claim: Some object to the accusative because a delimited place normally requires fi, while others allow it because the expression remains semantically open.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r6.anchor: وتعقب القول بانتصابهما مطلقا بأنهما محدودان ومحدود المكان لابد له من في وبعضهم يجوز النصب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r7.claim: A nominative parsing is also proposed: the two forms can be subjects governed by the adverb, or coordinated subjects with bismi llah as predicate and an omitted predicate understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r7.anchor: وجوز رفعهما فاعلين بالظرف لإعتماده على ذي الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r8.claim: The sentence can resume the discourse: Noah first orders boarding, then assures them that sailing and landing occur by God's name, encouraging them and easing fear of drowning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r8.anchor: والجملة إما مقتضية منقطعة عما قبلها لإختلافهما خبرا وطلبا على أن نوحا عليه السلام أمرهم بالركوب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that Noah said bismi llah when setting the Ark in motion and again when bringing it to rest.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r9.anchor: ويروى عن الضحاك أنه عليه السلام كان إذا أراد أن يجريها يقول ( بسم الله ) فتجري وإذا أراد أن يرسيها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r10.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is a prospective circumstantial clause describing the Ark as sailing and settling by God's name.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r10.anchor: وهي حال مقدرة إذ لا إجراء ولا إرساء وقت الركوب كذا قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r11.speaker: التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r11.claim: Al-Taqrib objects that a clause cannot be a prospective circumstantial phrase: the wording implies sailing by God's name occurs while they board.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r11.anchor: وتعقبه في التقريب بأن الحال إنما تكون مقدرة إذا كانت مفردة كمجراة أما إذا كانت جملة فلا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r12.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r12.claim: Al-Kashf answers that a clause can be prospective too, comparing it with entering Paradise while destined to remain there.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r12.anchor: وأجاب عنه في الكشف بأنه لا فرق بين قوله تعالى : ( ادخلوها خالدين )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r13.claim: Al-Alusi says the response misses al-Taqrib's point: a clause implies realized, continuing involvement, so a pending event is awkward when a single-word circumstantial phrase is available.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r13.anchor: فإنهم ذكروا أن الفرق بين الحال إذا كانت مفردة وإذا كانت جملة أن الثانية تقتضي التحقق في نفسها والتلبس بها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r14.claim: Making the phrase a prospective circumstantial clause of the riders is challenged because it lacks a link to them and requires a strained nominal paraphrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r14.anchor: وجوز أن تكون حالا مقدرة أيضا من فاعل ( اركبوا ) واعترض بأنه لا عائد على ذي الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r15.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r15.claim: Al-Radi allows a nominal circumstantial clause to lack both usual links when the relation of accompaniment is obvious.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r15.anchor: والقول بأن الرضي قد ذكر أن الجملة الحالية إذا كانت اسمية قد تخلو من الرابطين عند ظهور الملابسة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r16.claim: Al-Alusi says the appeal to al-Radi is unsound here, and rejects as overbroad the rules that nominal circumstantials must always have waw and that prospective circumstantials cannot be clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r16.anchor: نعم كون الإسمية لابد فيها من الواو والقول بأن الحال المقدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r17.claim: A further parsing treats the word name as an inserted element, as in Labid's line; by God then means by His power, command, or permission, with metaphorical attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p56/r17.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الإسم مقحما كما في قول لبيد : فقوما وقولا بالذي قد عرفتما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r1.claim: Most readers pronounce majraha and mursaha with an open mīm as verbal nouns, time-nouns, or place-nouns from the triliteral verbs jara and rasa.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r1.anchor: وقرأ مجراها ومرساها بفتح الميم مصدرين أو زمانين أو مكانين على أنهما من جرى ورسا الثلاثيين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r2.claim: Mujahid reads the forms as active participles, mujriha and mursiha.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد مجريها ومرسيها بصيغة اسم الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqaʾ parses Mujahid's forms as adjectives modifying the divine name.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r3.anchor: وخرج ذلك أبو البقاء على أنهما صفتان للاسم الجليل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r4.claim: The adjective analysis is challenged because a future active participle has a non-definite annexation and cannot modify a definite noun; badal is the sounder parsing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r4.anchor: إن إضافة اسم الفاعل إذا كان بمعنى المستقبل لفظية فهو نكرة لا يصح توصيف المعرفة به فالحق البدلية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r5.claim: Calling the adjective a semantic rather than syntactic description is judged a far-fetched response to the objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r5.anchor: والقول بأن مراد المعرب الصفة المعنوية لا النعت النحوي فلا ينافي البدلية بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r6.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r6.claim: Al-Khalil allows a normally incomplete annexation to become complete and definite, except for the annexation of an adjective of inherent quality.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r6.anchor: لكن عن الخليل أن ما كانت إضافته غير محضة قد يصح أن تجعل محضة فتعرف إلا ما كان من الصفة المشبهة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r7.claim: Rusu means firmness and stability; an unnamed poet's line uses it of a steadfast soul when the coward's soul is unsettled.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r7.anchor: والرسو الثبوت والإستقرار ومنه قول الشاعر : فصبرت نفسا عند ذلك حرة ( ترسو ) إذا نفس الجبان تطلع

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r8.claim: The closing clause explains why they were saved: without God's forgiveness and mercy, their faith would not merit rescue from the calamity, which accords with Sunni teaching that rescue is sheer grace.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r8.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن نجاتهم لم تكن عن استحقاق بسبب أنهم كانوا مؤمنين بل بمحض رحمة الله تعالى وغفرانه على ما عليه أهل السنة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r9.claim: The closing clause cannot directly justify the order to board because the required causal relation is absent unless an unstated rationale is supplied.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r9.anchor: ومنع صلاحية كونها علة لاركبوا لعدم المناسبة فيقدر ما يصح به الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r10.claim: One supplied rationale is: obey this command so God may save you through forgiveness and mercy; another is to invoke God and fear no drowning because He is forgiving and merciful.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r10.anchor: بأن يقال : متثلوا هذا الحكم لينجيكم من الهلاك بمغفرته ورحمته

ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r11.claim: Some make the clause a reason for boarding because it alludes to the passengers' eventual salvation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p57/r11.anchor: وجعلها بعضهم تعليلا بالنظر إلى ما فيها من الإشارة إلى النجاة فكأنه قيل : اركبوا لينجيكم الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r1.claim: Board means enter; the action is called riding because the vessel moves in water like a mount moves on land.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r1.anchor: أي صيروا فيها وجعل ذلك ركوبا لأنها في الماء كالمركوب في الأرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r2.claim: In the phrase In God's name is its course and anchorage, the phrase may attach to the command as a circumstantial clause: board while naming God, or while saying it at departure and landing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r2.anchor: متصل ب { اركبوا } حال من الواو أي اركبوا فيها مسمين الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r3.claim: The course and anchorage may denote time, place, or verbal noun with an omitted noun; they can be accusative as a circumstantial construction or nominative governed by In God's name.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r3.anchor: على أن المجرى والمرسى للوقت أو المكان أو المصدر، والمضاف محذوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r4.claim: Alternatively, the wording may be a complete nominal sentence, an independent sentence, or an anticipatory circumstantial clause connected to the people or vessel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r4.anchor: أو جملة من مبتدأ وخبر، أي إجراؤها { بسم الله }

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r5.claim: A report says Noah said In God's name whenever he wanted the Ark to move, and it moved; he said it when he wished it to anchor, and it anchored.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r5.anchor: وروي أنه كان إذا أراد أن تجري قال بسم الله فجرت

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r6.claim: The word ism may be an added particle, as in the cited poetic line, Then the name of peace be upon you both.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الاسم مقحما كقوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r7.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and ʿĀṣim through Ḥafṣ read مجراها with fatḥa; it is also read مرسها with fatḥa. Each can bear three grammatical meanings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وعاصم برواية حفص { مجراها } بالفتح من جرى

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r8.claim: مجريها and مرسيها as active participles are descriptions of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r8.anchor: و «مجريها ومرسيها» بلفظ الفاعل صفتين لله

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r9.claim: Noah acknowledges that God's forgiveness of their lapses and mercy toward them were necessary for their rescue.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:41/r9.anchor: أي لولا مغفرته لفرطاتكم ورحمته إياكم لما نجاكم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r1.claim: Noah promptly gathered those commanded into the vessel and told them to board; فيها suits the vessel because spatial containment is the usual relation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r1.anchor: بادر الامتثال فجمع من أمره الله به إلى السفينة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r2.claim: The phrase “In God's name is its course and anchorage” may be Noah's own statement or the words he tells the passengers to say; it names movement, stopping, and their place and time.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r2.anchor: استأنف قوله , أو أمرهم بالركوب قائلين : { بسم الله } أي الذي له الإحاطة الكاملة { مجراها ومرساها } أي إجرائها وإرساءها ومحلهما ووقتهمان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وحميد العرج وإسماعيل بن مجالد عن عاصم
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r3.claim: These readers pronounce rāʾ and sīn with full kasrah followed by two clear yāʾs, treating both forms as adjectives of the divine name.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة وحميد العرج وإسماعيل بن مجالد عن عاصم بكسر الراء والسين كسرا خالصا بعده ياءان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r4.claim: Noah attributes their salvation to God's forgiveness, since there is no rescue apart from His pardon; غفور and رحيم stress covering faults and granting honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r4.anchor: اعترافا بأنه لا نجاة إلا بعفوه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r5.claim: The ark's passage over mountain-like waves is miraculous, and the image conveys their height, mass, and accumulation.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p531/r5.anchor: فكان السير على ظهره من الخوارق , وأشار إلى ذلك بالظرف فقال : { في موج } ونبه على علوه بقوله : { كالجبال }

AKHFASH:v1p382/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p382/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p382/r3.claim: مجرىها and مرساها can derive from the form أجريت and أرسيت.
AKHFASH:v1p382/r3.anchor: [وقال] {وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجرياها ومرساها} اذا جعلت من "أجريت" و"أرسيت"

AKHFASH:v1p382/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p382/r4.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p382/r4.claim: Some derive مجراها and مرساها from the basic verbs جريت and رست.
AKHFASH:v1p382/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم (مجراها ومرساها) اذا جعلت من "جريت"

AKHFASH:v1p382/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p382/r5.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p382/r5.claim: Some read مجريها ومرسيها as descriptions of God, making Him the one who causes it to sail and moor.
AKHFASH:v1p382/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم (مجريها ومرسيها) لانه أراد ان يجعل ذلك صفة لله عز وجل

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r1.claim: Noah boarded during the first ten days of Rajab and left the ark during the first ten days of Muharram, fasting with his family from dusk to dusk.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال : ركب في السفينة في عشر خلت من رجب ونزل عنها في عشر خلت من المحرم فصام هو واهله من الليل إلى الليل

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r2.claim: Abu Salih says Noah boarded with his three sons, wife, and the sons' three wives, totaling eight; the sons were Japheth, Ham, and Sam.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r2.anchor: ان أبا صالح اخبره ان نوحا عليه السلام حمل معه بنيه الثلاثة وامراة نوح والثلاثة نسوة نساء بنيه الثلاث فهم ثمانية وازواجهم فاسماء بنيه يافث وحام وسام

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r3.claim: He says Ham had intercourse with his wife aboard, so Noah prayed for his offspring's complexion to change, and the Sudanese resulted.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r3.anchor: فاصاب حام امراته في السفينة فدعا نوح ان يغير لطفته فجاء السودان

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r4.claim: Another report gives eighty men with their families and a 150-day voyage.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان مع نوح في السفينة ثمانون رجلا معهم اهلوهم وانهم كانوا في السفينة مائة وخمسين يوما

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r5.claim: The ark was directed to Mecca, circled the Kaaba for forty days, then was directed to Mount Judi and settled there.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r5.anchor: وان الله وجه السفينة إلى مكة فدارت بالبيت اربعين يوما ثم وجهها إلى الجودي فاستقرت عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r6.claim: Noah first sent a raven, which landed on carrion and delayed; a dove returned with an olive leaf and mud on its feet, showing the water had receded.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r6.anchor: فبعث نوح الغراب لياتيه بخبر الأرض فذهب فوقع على الحيف فابطا عليه فبعث الحمامة فاتته بورق زيتون ولطخت رجليها بالطين

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r7.claim: Noah built a village at the foot of Judi called Eighty; its inhabitants' tongues divided into eighty languages, including Arabic, and Noah interpreted among them.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r7.anchor: فهبط إلى اسفل الجودي فبنى قرية وسماها ثمانين فاصبحوا ذات يوم وقد تبلبلت السنتهم على ثمانين لغة احدها اللسان العربي

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r8.speaker: جابر بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r8.claim: He calls Allah the Greatest Name, arguing that it begins before every other name throughout the Qur'an.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r8.anchor: عن أبي الشعثاء عن جابر بن زيد قوله : بسم الله قال : اسم الله الاعظم هو الله الا ترى انه في جميع القران يبدا قبل كل اسم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r9.claim: He assigns the basmala's letters to God's splendor, glory, and sovereignty, and says Allah is the deity of creation.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r9.anchor: عن جويبر عن الضحاك في قوله : بسم الله قال : الباء من بهاء الله والسين من سناء الله والميم من ملك الله والله يااله الخلق

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r1.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r1.claim: He reports that the Prophet wrote four documents, the first beginning 'In Your name, O God'; then Hud's surah was revealed with 'In God's name is its sailing and mooring.'
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي قال : كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اربعة كتب اولها باسمك اللهم قال : فنزلت سورة هود : بسم الله مجراها ومرساها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r2.claim: Noah said 'In God's name is its sailing' when he wanted the ark to move and 'its mooring' when he wanted it to stop.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : بسم الله مجراها ومرساها قال : كان اذا اراد ان تجري قال : بسم الله مجراها جرت واذا اراد ان تقف

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r3.claim: He glosses 'In God's name' as said when boarding, with the remaining words referring to sailing and mooring.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : بسم الله حين تركبون يعني مجراها ومرساها حين تجرون

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r4.claim: He advises passengers to recall God's favor and recite Noah's words when boarding; on an animal, one should mention God's name.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : اذا ركبت في السفينة يذكر نعمة الله وان شاء قال كما قال نوح صلى الله عليه وسلم بسم الله مجراها ومرساها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r5.claim: He says Satan urges a person who rides without invoking God to sing, and if he does not sing, to walk.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r5.anchor: فمن ركب دابة لم يذكر اسم الله جاء الشيطان فيقول تغنى فان لم يتغنى يقول له : تمشى

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r6.speaker: رزين بن حبيش
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r6.claim: He says the ark moored at the site by Kufa's Kinda gate, explaining why he prayed there on Fridays.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r6.anchor: رايت رزين بن حبيش يصلي في الزاوية حين تدخل من ابواب كندة عن يمينك فسالته انك لكثير الصلاة يوم الجمعة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r7.claim: He explains 'forgiving, merciful' as forgiveness for their former idolatry and mercy after their repentance.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : لغفور رحيم لما كان منهم في الشرك رحيم بهم بعد التوبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r1.claim: The command to board is attached to God's order to carry them; Nuh then addresses the people he was ordered to take aboard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة { قلنا احمل فيها } ( هود : 40 ) أي قلنا له ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r2.claim: Fiha refers implicitly to the ship, as in the description of the ark as a vessel of planks and nails.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r2.anchor: وضمير { فيها } لمفهوم من المقام ، أي السفينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r3.claim: Riding an animal takes ala, while boarding a ship takes fi because ship-riding is metaphorical: passengers sit and settle inside it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r3.anchor: وعدي فعل { اركبوا } ب ( في ) جريا على الفصيح فإنه يقال : ركب الدابة إذا علاها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r4.claim: The ba in bismillah marks accompaniment and is circumstantial of the addressees: they board while invoking God's name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r4.anchor: والباء في { باسم الله } للملابسة مثل ما تقدم في تفسير البسملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r5.claim: The majority pronounce the first vowel of both majraha and marsaha with damma; both are verbal nouns for making the ship sail and bringing it to rest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r5.anchor: و { مجراها ومرساها } بضم الميمين فيهما في قراءة الجمهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r6.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Hafs from Asim, and Khalaf read majraha with fatha as a verbal noun or time or place noun; marsaha remains with damma to avoid confusion with a mooring place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص عن عاصم ، وخلف ( مجراها ) فقط بفتح الميم على أنه مفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r7.claim: Majraha and marsaha may function as accusative time adverbs, or as nominative subjects licensed by the prepositional phrase's verbal force, a plausible Kufan analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { مجراها ومرساها } في محل نصب بالنيابة عن ظرف الزمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r8.claim: Nuh's assurance that God is forgiving and merciful explains boarding with God's name and hints that God promised their rescue; emphatic particles reassure his followers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p73/r8.anchor: وجملة { إن ربي لغفور رحيم } تعليل للأمر بالركوب المقيد بالملابسة لذكر اسم الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p74/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p74/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p74/r1.claim: The description of the ship surging in mountain-like waves is parenthetical, completing the mention of its sailing and showing the day's grandeur and God's wondrous rescue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p74/r1.anchor: جملة معترضة دعا إلى اعتراضها هنا ذكر ( مجراها ) إتماما للفائدة وصفا لعظم اليوم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r1.claim: Majrāhā means the ship's course or journey.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r2.claim: Marsāhā means where it is moored or comes to rest; the related verb can also mean to stop.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r2.anchor: حيث ترسى وترسو أيضا. أي: تقف.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r1.claim: When Noah was told to carry the believers aboard, he told them to board; the feminine pronoun refers to the ship, although fulk is grammatically masculine.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r1.anchor: المعنى وقال نوح- حين أمر بالحمل في السفينة- لمن آمن معه: اركبوا فيها فأنث الضمير، إذ هي سفينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r2.speaker: أبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r2.claim: Ubayy's codex reads “ʿalā ismi Allāh” in place of “bi-smi Allāh.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r3.claim: One parsing makes bi-smi Allāh a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in “board”: board seeking God's blessing; majrāhā and mursāhā are temporal adverbs for sailing and mooring, governed by the verbal sense of the basmala.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: بسم الله يصح أن يكون في موضع الحال من الضمير الذي في قوله: اركبوا كما تقول: خرج زيد بثيابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r4.claim: Another parsing makes bi-smi Allāh the predicate and majrāhā/mursāhā verbal nouns as subject: the ship's sailing and mooring occur by God's blessing; the sentence is circumstantial with the pronoun in “therein.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r4.anchor: ويصح أن يكون قوله: بسم الله في موضع خبر ومجراها ومرساها ابتداء مصدران كأنه قال: اركبوا فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r5.claim: The second parsing cannot be a circumstantial clause attached to the command “board,” because it contains no pronoun referring back to that command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r5.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون حالا من الضمير في قوله: اركبوا لأنه لا عائد في الجملة يعود عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says Noah said the basmala whenever he wanted the ship to move or stop, and it responded accordingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا التأويل قال الضحاك: إن نوحا كان إذا أراد جري السفينة قال: بسم الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim in Abu Bakr's transmission, and Ibn ʿAmir read both forms with ḍamma on the mīm, as verbal nouns for sailing and mooring; many other authorities also read this way, and Labid supplies poetic evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم- في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر: «مجراها ومرساها» بضم الميمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r8.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim read majrāhā with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the rāʾ, while retaining ḍamma in mursāhā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: «مجراها» بفتح الميم وكسر الراء، وكلهم ضم الميم من «مرساها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r9.speaker: الأعمش وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Masʿud read both words with fatḥa on their mīms, treating them as places of running and settling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وابن مسعود «مجراها ومرساها» بفتح الميمين، وذلك من الجري والرسو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r1.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r1.claim: Al-Tabari chooses the reading of majrāhā with fatḥa on the first mīm and ḍamma on the second, arguing from “it sails”; Ibn Masʿud also read the phrase, transmitted by Abu Waʾil and Masruq.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r1.anchor: واختار الطبري قراءة «مجراها» بفتح الميم الأولى وضم الثانية، ورجحها بقوله تعالى: وهي تجري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r2.speaker: ابن وثاب وأبو رجاء العطاري والنخعي والجحدري والكلبي والضحاك بن مزاحم ومسلم بن جندب وأهل الشام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r2.claim: These readers say mujrihā and mursīhā, two active-participle attributes of God, referring back to God in “in the name of God.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وأبو رجاء العطاري والنخعي والجحدري والكلبي والضحاك بن مزاحم ومسلم بن جندب وأهل الشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r3.claim: The statement “my Lord is forgiving, merciful” reminds the believers of God's blessings, mercy, concealment, and forgiveness of their sins upon their repentance and return to Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r3.anchor: وقوله إن ربي لغفور رحيم تنبيه لهم على قدر نعم الله عليهم ورحمته لهم وستره عليهم وغفرانه ذنوبهم بتوبتهم وإنابتهم

MAJAZ:v1p289/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p289/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p289/r1.claim: Majrāhā means its course or journey, from “it ran with them”; another reading takes it from ajraytuhā, “I made it run.”
MAJAZ:v1p289/r1.anchor:
«بسم الله مجراها» (41) أي مسيرها وهى من جرت بهم، ومن قال:
مجراها جعله من أجريتها أنا،

MAJAZ:v1p289/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p289/r2.claim: Labīd’s verse uses mujra Dāḥis for the race or course of Dāḥis; ḥarsan means a long duration.
MAJAZ:v1p289/r2.anchor:
قال لبيد:
وعمرت حرسا قبل مجرى داحس ... لو كان للنفس اللجوج خلود

MAJAZ:v1p289/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p289/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p289/r3.claim: Mursāhā means its stopping place, the verbal noun of arsāytuhā, “I moored it.”
MAJAZ:v1p289/r3.anchor: «ومرساها» (41) أي وقفها وهو مصدر أرسيتها أنا.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r1.claim: Noah addressed those he had been ordered to carry and told them to board the ark.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وقال ﴾ يعني نوحا للذين أمر بحملهم ﴿ اركبوا ﴾ السفينة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r2.claim: One report says they boarded on 10 Rajab and left the ark on ʿĀshūrāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ركبوا فيها لعشر مضين من رجب وخرجوا منها يوم عاشوراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r3.claim: The ark rose from ʿAyn Warda on Friday, 10 Rajab, circled the site of the raised Kaʿba seven times, and landed at Baqardā on al-Jūdī on ʿĀshūrāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج رفعت من عين وردة يوم الجمعة لعشر مضين من رجب فأتت موضع البيت فطافت به أسبوعا وكان البيت قد رفع في ذلك الوقت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r4.claim: When a mouse gnawed the ark’s ropes, God inspired Noah to rub a lion’s tail, producing two cats.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس قرض الفأر حبال السفينة فشكا نوح ذلك فأوحى الله تعالى إليه فمسح ذنب الأسد فخرج سنوران

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r5.claim: A further story says Noah complained about the filth; after God’s instruction he rubbed the elephant’s tail, and two pigs emerged and ate it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r5.anchor: وكان في السفينة عذرة فشكا ذلك إلى ربه فأوحى الله تعالى إليه فمسح ذنب الفيل فيخرج خنزيران فأكلا ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r6.claim: Readers differ on the vowels of majrāhā and marsāhā: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr read majrāhā with ḍamma on mīm; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read it with fatḥa mīm and kasra rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبوبكر عن عاصم مجراها بضم الميم وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم مجراها بفتح الميم وكسر الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r7.claim: All read marsāhā with ḍamma mīm; Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ open sīn, while Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr use an intermediate pronunciation and Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf incline it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r7.anchor: وكلهم قرؤوا بضم الميم من مرساها إلا أن ابن كثير وأبا عمرو وابن عامر وحفصا عن عاصم كانوا يفتحون السين ونافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم كانا يقرآنها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r8.speaker: الحسن، قتادة، حميد الأعرج، إسماعيل بن مجالد عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r8.claim: These authorities alone make the two participles divine attributes, reading mujrihā and mursihā with ḍamma mīm and two yāʾs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r8.anchor: وإنما جعل الوصفين نعتا لله تعالى الحسن وقتادة وحميد الأعرج وإسماعيل بن مجالد عن عاصم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads majrāhā with fatḥa mīm and imāla on rāʾ, and marsāhā with raised mīm and imāla on sīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود مجراها بفتح الميم وإمالة الراء بعدها ألف ومرساها برفع الميم وإمالة السين بعدها ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r10.speaker: أبو رزين، أبو المتوكل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r10.claim: They read majrāhā with fatḥa on mīm and rāʾ, and marsāhā with raised mīm and fatḥa sīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين وأبوالمتوكل مجراها بفتح الميم والراء وبألف بعدها ومرساها برفع الميم وفتح السين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r11.speaker: أبو الجوزاء، ابن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r11.claim: They read both words with fatḥa on mīm and on rāʾ or sīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو الجوزاء وابن يعمر مجراها ومرساها بفتح الميم فيهما جميعا وفتح الراء والسين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r12.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r12.claim: He opens both mīms but applies imāla to both rāʾ and sīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب بفتح الميمين إلا أنه أمال الراء والسين فيهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r13.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني، ابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r13.claim: They raise both mīms and open rāʾ and sīn, followed by alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمران الجوني وابن جبير برفع الميم فيهما وفتح الراء والسين وبألف بعدهما جميعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r14.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r14.claim: With ḍamma mīm the forms derive from أجرى and أرسى; with fatḥa mīm they are verbal nouns from jarā and rasā.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r14.anchor: فمن قرأ بضم الميمين جعله من أجرى وأرسى ومن فتحهما جعله مصدرا من جرى الشيء يجري مجرى ورسى يرسي مرسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r15.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r15.claim: By God’s name means by God; Noah told them to name God when the ark moved and when it came to rest.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r15.anchor: قال الزجاج قوله ﴿ بسم الله ﴾ أي بالله والمعنى أنه أمرهم أن يسموا في وقت جريها ووقت استقرارها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r1.claim: Noah says the ark's movement across the water and its final anchoring both occur in God's name.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r1.anchor: أي: بسم الله يكون جريها على وجه الماء، وبسم الله يكون منتهى سيرها، وهو رسوها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r2.claim: Abu Raja al-Ataridi reads the two words in the form mujriha and mursiha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي: "بسم الله مجريها ومرسيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r3.claim: The instruction links with the prayer to praise God after reaching safety and to ask for a blessed landing; Ibn Kathir accordingly recommends naming God when beginning to ride a ship or animal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r3.anchor: ولهذا تستحب التسمية في ابتداء الأمور: عند الركوب على السفينة وعلى الدابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r4.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas says protection from drowning while aboard ships comes by invoking God's name, reciting the verse about God's grasp of the earth and heavens, then Noah's formula.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322/r4.anchor: قال: "أمان أمتي من الغرق إذا ركبوا في السفن أن يقولوا: بسم الله الملك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r1.claim: The mention of God's forgiveness and mercy suits the preceding destruction of unbelievers, since other verses pair His vengeance with mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {إن ربي لغفور رحيم} مناسب عند

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r2.claim: The ark sailed over water covering the whole earth and rising above mountain peaks; reports give its height as fifteen cubits or eighty miles.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r2.anchor: خمسة عشر ذراعا، وقيل: بثمانين ميلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r3.claim: The ark moved by God's permission and under His care and protection, as other verses describe the saved being carried in the ship under divine watch.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p322#2/r3.anchor: وهذه السفينة على وجه الماء سائرة بإذن الله وتحت كنفه وعنايته

NAHHAS:v2p282/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p282/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p282/r8.claim: The two mīms are ḍamma in the reading of the two sanctuaries and Basrans except a few; al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī open the mīm of majrāhā and round that of marsāhā.
NAHHAS:v2p282/r8.anchor: بضم ميميهما قراءة أهل الحرمين وأهل البصرة إلا من شذ منهم وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي ( بسم الله مجراها )

NAHHAS:v2p282/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p282/r9.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
NAHHAS:v2p282/r9.claim: A report through Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā gives Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb's reading with both mīms open.
NAHHAS:v2p282/r9.anchor: وروي عن يحيى بن عيسى عن الأعمش عن يحيى بن وثاب ( باسم الله مجراها ومرساها ) بفتح الميم فيهما

NAHHAS:v2p282/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p282/r10.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v2p282/r10.claim: Mujāhid, Muslim ibn Jundub, and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read mujrihā and mursīhā.
NAHHAS:v2p282/r10.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ومسلم بن جندب وعاصم الجحدري ( باسم الله مجريها ومرسيها )

NAHHAS:v2p282/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p282/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p282/r11.claim: The first reading means by God's name its running and anchoring; marsāhā is nominative as a subject or may be accusative meaning at the time it runs.
NAHHAS:v2p282/r11.anchor: فالقراءة الأولى بمعنى باسم الله إجراؤها وإرساؤها مرفوع بالابتداء ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب ويكون التقدير باسم الله وقت إجرائها

NAHHAS:v2p282/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p282/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p282/r12.claim: Another parse supplies mawḍiʿ, meaning in God's name is the place of its movement, then omits mawḍiʿ and uses majrāhā in its place.
NAHHAS:v2p282/r12.anchor: وقيل التقدير باسم الله موضع إجرائها ثم حذف موضع وأقيم مجراها مقامه

NAHHAS:v2p282/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p282/r13.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v2p282/r13.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says that when Noah said in God's name, the ark moved, and when he said in God's name, it came to rest.
NAHHAS:v2p282/r13.anchor: وقال الضحاك كان إذا قال باسم الله جرت وإذا قال باسم الله رست

NAHHAS:v2p282/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p282/r14.speaker: author
