NAHHAS:v2p282/r14.claim: The bāʾ attaches to irkabū; the open-mīm forms derive from running and settling, while mujrihā and mursīhā may be God's genitive adjectives, an implied nominative, or accusatives of state.
NAHHAS:v2p282/r14.anchor: ومجريها نعت لله جل وعز في موضع جر ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع على إضمار مبتدأ أي هو مجريها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r10.claim: One construction joins 'in God's name' to 'ride' as a circumstantial phrase: they ride naming God or saying the basmala at sailing and anchoring, whether understood as times or verbal nouns with an omitted time noun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r10.anchor: أن يتصل { بسم الله } باركبوا حالا من الواو ، بمعنى : اركبوا فيها مسمين الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r11.claim: Alternatively, the two words refer to places of setting out and anchoring, governed by the verbal meaning of the basmala or by an implied act of saying.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد مكانا الإجراء والإرساء ، وانتصابهما بما في { بسم الله } من معنى الفعل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r12.claim: A second construction makes 'In God's name is its sailing and anchoring' a complete subject-predicate sentence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r12.anchor: أن يكون { بسم الله مجراها ومرساها } جملة من مبتدأ وخبر مقتضيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r13.claim: It is related that whenever Noah wanted the ark to sail or settle, he said 'In God's name,' and it then sailed or anchored.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p373#2/r13.anchor: يروى أنه كان إذا أراد أن تجري قال : بسم الله فجرت ، وإذا أراد أن ترسو قال

MUJAHID:v1p304/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p304/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p304/r1.claim: The words about sailing and mooring in God's name mean invoking God when boarding, sailing, and coming to rest.
MUJAHID:v1p304/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وقال اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها ﴾ يعني سموا الله حين تركبون وحين تجرون وحين ترسون

MUJAHID:v1p304/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p304/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p304/r2.claim: The water's subsiding means that it decreased.
MUJAHID:v1p304/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وغيض الماء ﴾ يعني نقص الماء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r1.claim: The basmala can attach to the command to board as a circumstantial phrase: they board while naming God or say it when the ship starts and comes to rest.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r1.anchor: بسم الله متصل باركوا حالا من الواو أى اركبوا فيها مسمين الله أو قائلين بسم الله وقت إجرائها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r2.claim: The time expressions may be nouns of time, or verbal nouns with an omitted genitive referring to the time of starting and mooring.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r2.anchor: اما لأن المجرى والمرسى للوقت واما لانهما مصدران كالاجراء والارساء حذف منهما الوقت المضاف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, the basmala clause stands independently as subject and predicate, explaining that the ship’s movement and anchoring occur through God’s name; Noah said it at each moment.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بسم الله مجراها ومرساها جملة برأسها غير متعلقة بما قبلها وهى مبتدأ وخبر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r4.speaker: حمزة وعلى وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r4.claim: Hamzah, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read the word for its course with fatḥa on mīm and kasra on rāʾ; Abū ʿAmr has kasra on rāʾ with mīm ḍamma, and the rest have both letters ḍamma.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r4.anchor: مجريها بفتح الميم وكسر الراء من جرى اما مصدر أو وقت حمزة وعلى وحفص

NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r5.claim: God is forgiving to the believers aboard and merciful in delivering them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p154#3/r5.anchor: ﴿ إن ربي لغفور ﴾ لمن امن منهم ﴿ رحيم ﴾ حيث خلصهم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r1.claim: The command 'board' may be spoken by God or by Noah to his people; rakiba literally means to mount something.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r1.anchor: أمر بالركوب ويحتمل أن يكون من الله تعالى، ويحتمل أن يكون من نوح لقومه. والركوب العلو على ظهر الشيء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r2.claim: The phrase has an ellipsis: board the water in the ship; another explanation is simply 'board it.'
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r2.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف أي اركبوا الماء في السفينة. وقيل: المعنى اركبوها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r3.claim: The preposition fī may be emphatic, as in 12:43; it also ensures they enter the ship's interior rather than ride on its roof.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r3.anchor: وفائدة «في» أنهم أمروا أن يكونوا في جوفها لا على ظهرها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r4.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r4.claim: ʿIkrima dates Noah's boarding to the tenth of Rajab and the ark's settling on al-Jūdī to the tenth of Muḥarram, six months later.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r4.anchor: قال عكرمة: ركب نوح عليه السلام في الفلك لعشر خلون من رجب، واستوت على الجودي لعشر خلون من المحرم فذلك ستة أشهر

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r5.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r5.claim: Qatāda agrees on the dates and adds that the landing was ʿĀshūrāʾ; Noah told those aboard to finish or begin fasting that day.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r5.anchor: فذلك ستة أشهر وقاله قتادة وزاد وهو يوم عاشوراء فقال لمن كان معه: من كان صائما فليتم صومه، ومن لم يكن صائما فليصمه

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a prophetic report that Noah boarded on the first of Rajab, fasted the whole month, sailed until ʿĀshūrāʾ, and landed on al-Jūdī, where he and his companions fasted.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r6.anchor: وذكر الطبري في هذا حديثا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن نوحا ركب في السفينة أول يوم من رجب، وصام الشهر أجمع، وجرت بهم السفينة إلى يوم عاشوراء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r7.speaker: ابن إسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites Ibn Isḥāq as implying that the ark remained on the water about a year, circled the raised, un-flooded House seven times, went to Yemen, then returned to al-Jūdī.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r7.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن ابن إسحق ما يقتضي أنه أقام على الماء نحو السنة، ومرت بالبيت فطافت به سبعا، وقد رفعه الله عن الغرق فلم ينله غرق، ثم مضت إلى اليمن ورجعت إلى الجودي

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r8.speaker: قراءة أهل الحرمين وأهل البصرة
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r8.claim: The people of Mecca, Medina, and Basra read both words with ḍamma on mīm, meaning the ark's sailing and anchoring; the forms are nominative as a beginning or accusative with an implied 'time.'
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r8.anchor: قراءة أهل الحرمين وأهل البصرة بضم الميم فيهما إلا من شذ، على معنى بسم الله إجراؤها وإرساؤها فمجراها ومرساها في موضع رفع بالابتداء ويجوز أن تكون في موضع نصب، ويكون التقدير: بسم الله وقت إجرائها

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r9.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r9.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read mujrihā with fatḥa and mursāhā with ḍamma.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي: «بسم الله مجريها» بفتح الميم و «مرساها» بضم الميم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r10.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r10.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, through al-Aʿmash, reads both words with fatḥa as verbal nouns of 'to flow' and 'to settle.'
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r10.anchor: وروى يحيى بن عيسى عن الأعمش عن يحيى بن وثاب «بسم الله مجراها ومرساها» بفتح الميم فيهما على المصدر من جرت تجري جريا ومجرى، ورست رسوا ومرسى

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r11.speaker: مجاهد وسليمان بن جندب وعاصم الجحدري وأبو رجاء العطاردي
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r11.claim: These readers use the forms mujrihā and mursīhā as adjectives of God, construed in genitive, nominative with an implied subject, or accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r11.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وسليمان بن جندب وعاصم الجحدري وأبو رجاء العطاردي: «بسم الله مجريها ومرسيها» نعت لله عز وجل في موضع جر. ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع على إضمار مبتدأ أي هو مجريها ومرسيها. ويجوز النصب على الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r12.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r12.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the ark moved when Noah said 'In God's name, its sailing' and stopped when he said 'In God's name, its anchoring.'
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r12.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كان نوح عليه السلام إذا قال بسم الله مجراها جرت، وإذا قال بسم الله مرساها رست

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r13.claim: A report through Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī says that saying 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate' when boarding a ship protects the Prophet's community from drowning.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41/r13.anchor: وروى مروان بن سالم عن طلحة بن عبيد الله بن كريز عن الحسين بن علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r1.claim: Qurṭubī connects the basmala aboard the ark with the verse describing God's grasp of the earth and folding of the heavens.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r1.anchor: بسم الله مجراها ومرساها إن ربي لغفور رحيم

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r2.claim: This verse supports saying the basmala at the start of every action, as discussed under the basmala.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r2.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل على ذكر البسملة عند ابتداء كل فعل كما بيناه في البسملة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r3.claim: 'My Lord is forgiving, merciful' refers to the people aboard the ship.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:41-42/r3.anchor: { إن ربي لغفور رحيم } أي لأهل السفينة

RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r1.claim: Possible grammatical governors of bi-smi Allah are ride in God's name, begin in God's name, or the statement that its sailing and anchoring are in God's name.
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r1.anchor: ذكروا في عامل الإعراب في { بسم الله } وجوها : الأول : اركبوا بسم الله

RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r2.claim: Reports say the ark set sail on the first of Rajab or after ten days of Rajab, floated for six months, and came to rest on al-Judi on the tenth of Muharram.
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنها سارت لأول يوم من رجب ، وقيل : لعشر مضين من رجب ، فصارت ستة أشهر

RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r3.claim: On one construction, Noah's command and the invocation form one sentence: boarding should begin with God's sacred name, so that remembrance at the start of every undertaking brings its completion through blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r3.anchor: والتقدير : وقال اركبوا فيها بسم مجريها ومرساها ، يعني ينبغي أن يكون الركوب مقرونا بهذا الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r4.claim: On a second construction there are two sentences: Noah orders boarding, then teaches that only God's name, command, and power make the ark sail and anchor; salvation comes through God's grace, not reliance on the boat.
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r4.anchor: أن مجريها ومرساها ليس إلا بسم الله وأمره وقدرته

RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r5.claim: The first construction places Noah in remembrance when boarding; the second places him in contemplation, disavowing independent power and created means while absorbed in the light of the Cause of causes.
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r5.anchor: فعلى التقدير الأول كان نوح عليه السلام وقت ركوب السفينة في مقام الذكر ، وعلى التقدير الثاني كان في مقام الفكر

RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r6.claim: Razi allegorizes the seeker of knowledge as sailing in a ship of reflection through waves of error; the heart and intellect must rely on God until the ship reaches the shore of salvation.
RAZI-FULL:v17p183/r6.anchor: إذا ابتدأت سفينة الفكرة والروية بالحركة وجب أن يكون هناك اعتماده على الله تعالى وتضرعه

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r1.claim: The subject of وقال may be Noah, or God speaking to Noah and those with him.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون الفاعل ضمير نوح عليه السلام

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r2.claim: فيها attaches to اركبوا; the preposition في is used because the verb implies enter while riding or travel within it.

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r3.claim: One proposed estimate is اركبوا الماء فيها.

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r4.claim: Another analysis treats في as extra for emphasis.

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r5.claim: بسم الله may be a circumstantial phrase from the subject of اركبوا or the pronoun in فيها; مجراها and مرساها then function as subjects of the implied stability in that phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون هذا الجار والمجرور حالا من فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r6.claim: Alternatively, بسم الله is a fronted predicate and مجراها a delayed subject, with the sentence as an estimated circumstantial clause, as Abū al-Baqāʾ and others parse it.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " بسم الله " خبرا مقدما

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r7.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r7.claim: Makkī objects that these circumstantial parses lack a linking pronoun returning to the subject of اركبوا; the pronoun in بسم الله links to مجراها, or to فيها under the relevant parse.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r7.anchor: إلا أن مكيا منع ذلك لخلو الجملة من ضمير

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r8.claim: Another parse makes بسم الله circumstantial and treats مجراها and مرساها as spatial or temporal adverbs: embark naming the location or time of sailing and mooring.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r8.anchor: في موضع الظرف المكاني أو الزماني

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r9.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r9.claim: Makkī says the adverbs' governing element is the implied stability in بسم الله, so the meaning is to embark invoking God's blessing at those places or times.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r9.anchor: والعامل في هذين الظرفين حينئذ ما تضمنه

SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r10.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r10.claim: Makkī rules out اركبوا as the adverbs' governor: the command is to name God at sailing and mooring, not to embark during those times.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41/r10.anchor: قال مكي: " ولا يجوز أن يكون العامل فيهما

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r1.claim: مجراها and مرساها may be verbal nouns raised by بسم الله as subjects, meaning their launching and mooring occur through God's name; then بسم الله can only be circumstantial from the pronoun in فيها.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r1.anchor: مصدرين، و " بسم الله " حال كما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r2.claim: With those parses the utterance is one sentence; it may instead be an independent clause about the vessel's movement and stopping being by God's name.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r2.anchor: جملة مستأنفة لا تعلق لها بالأولى من حيث الإعراب

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r3.claim: A transmitted interpretation says the ship stopped when he said بسم الله and moved when he said it intending to sail; both clauses are quoted under وقال.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r3.anchor: وقفت، وإذا قالها جرت عند إرادته ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r4.claim: The two Ḥijāzī readers and Ḥafṣ open the mīm of مجراها; the others use a damma.

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r5.claim: The seven readers agree on a damma in مرساها, while Ibn Masʿūd, ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī, Zayd b. ʿAlī, and al-Aʿmash read its mīm open.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r5.anchor: واتفق السبعة على ضم ميم " مرساها "

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r6.claim: The damma readings derive from أجرى and أرسى, while the fatha readings derive from جرت and رست; either can be a time or place adverb or a verbal noun under the earlier parses.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r6.anchor: فالضم فيهما لأنهما من أجرى وأرسى، والفتح لأنهما من جرت ورست

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and other readers use the active participles مجريها and مرسيها, parsed as appositions to the name of God.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r7.anchor: وهما اسما فاعلين من أجرى وأرسى، وتخريجهما

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, Abū al-Baqāʾ, and Makkī call these active participles adjectives of God; the author says this only works if the annexation becomes definite, which conflicts with al-Khalīl's rule for صفة مشبهة.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وأبو البقاء ومكي: إنهما نعتان لله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r9.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r9.claim: Makkī says they can instead stand in place of active participles as estimated circumstantial modifiers in the accusative from God's name; he calls this a difficult, notable problem.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#2/r9.anchor: وقال مكي: " ولو جعلت " مجراها " و " مرساها " في موضع اسم الفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r1.claim: وهي تجري may be an independent clause, a circumstantial clause from the hidden pronoun in بسم الله, or a circumstantial clause from an omitted element inferred from context.

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supplies the context: they embarked saying بسم الله, and the vessel was then moving with them.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r2.anchor: ولذلك فسره الزمخشري بقوله: " أي: تجري وهم فيها

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r3.anchor: وقوله: { بهم } يجوز فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يتعلق ب " تجري "

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, بهم attaches to an omitted element, meaning the vessel moves while carrying them.

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses تجري بهم as meaning that they are aboard the vessel.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r5.anchor: ولذلك فسره الزمخشري بقوله: " أي: تجري وهم فيها

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r6.claim: الرسو means becoming fixed and settled, from رسا يرسو and أرسيتُه.
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r6.anchor: والرسو: الثبات والاستقرار، يقال: رسا يرسو وأرسيته أنا

SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r7.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:11:41#3/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses ترسو to mean that a steadfast soul settles while a coward's soul stirs.

TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r1.claim: The account omits that Noah carried the people aboard; the previous command to load and the following “board” make that action understood.
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r1.anchor: فحملهم نوح فيها وقال لهم: اركبوا فيها. فاستغنى بدلالة قوله: {وقال اركبوا فيها} [هود: 41] عن حمله إياهم فيها

TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r2.speaker: قراء أهل المدينة والبصرة وبعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r2.claim: Most Medinan, Basran, and some Kufan readers pronounce both forms with ḍamma as verbal nouns from causative forms; each can be nominative as “its running and anchoring” or accusative as “at its running and anchoring.”
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r2.anchor: قرأته عامة قراء أهل المدينة والبصرة وبعض الكوفيين: «بسم الله مجراها ومرساها» بضم الميم في الحرفين كليهما

TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r3.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r3.claim: Most Kufan readers open the mīm of majrāhā and damma the mīm of marsāhā, deriving them from jarā and arsā; the same two syntactic parses apply.
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفيين: {بسم الله مجراها ومرساها} [هود: 41] بفتح الميم من «مجراها» ، وضمها من «مرساها»

TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r4.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r4.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads both as active participles describing God as the one who makes the ark run and anchors it; genitive is likelier, though accusative as a circumstantial is possible.
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي رجاء العطاردي أنه كان يقرأ ذلك: «بسم الله مجريها ومرسيها» بضم الميم فيهما، ويصيرهما نعتا لله

TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r5.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r5.claim: Some Kufans open both mīms, treating the words as the ark’s states of sailing and anchoring; al-Ṭabarī cites ʿAntarah’s use of tarsū as poetic evidence.
TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r5.anchor: عن بعض الكوفيين أنه قرأ ذلك: مجراها ومرساها "، بفتح الميم

TAB-FULL:v12p416/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī chooses fatḥa in majrāhā and ḍamma in marsāhā: the former matches the nearby “it sails” in 11:42, while the latter follows the reciters’ consensus.
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r1.anchor: والقراءة التي نختارها في ذلك قراءة من قرأ: {بسم الله مجراها} [هود: 41] بفتح الميم {ومرساها} [هود: 41] بضم الميم

TAB-FULL:v12p416/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r2.claim: Majrāhā means the ark’s passage, and marsāhā its stopping, which God causes.
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله {مجراها} [هود: 41] مسيرها {ومرساها} [هود: 41] وقفها، من وقفها الله وأرساها

TAB-FULL:v12p416/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r3.claim: Mujāhid reads both mīms with ḍamma.
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r3.anchor: وكان مجاهد يقرأ ذلك بضم الميم في الحرفين جميعا

TAB-FULL:v12p416/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r4.claim: Mujāhid explains the invocation as said when they board, sail, and dock.
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: «بسم الله مجراها ومرساها» قال: حين يركبون ويجرون ويرسون

TAB-FULL:v12p416/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says invoking God’s name makes the ark sail or anchor whenever Noah intends either action.
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: «اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها» قال: إذا أراد أن ترسي قال: بسم الله فأرست

TAB-FULL:v12p416/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r6.claim: God is forgiving to those who repent and return to Him, and merciful not to punish them after repentance.
TAB-FULL:v12p416/r6.anchor: وقوله: {إن ربي لغفور رحيم} [هود: 41] يقول: إن ربي لساتر ذنوب من تاب، وأناب إليه، رحيم بهم أن يعذبهم بعد التوبة

TABATABAI:11:41/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r1.speaker: قرئ
TABATABAI:11:41/r1.claim: Majrāhā with fatḥa on the mīm means the ship's course or sailing; with ḍamma it means causing the ship to run or steering it.
TABATABAI:11:41/r1.anchor: قرئ مجراها بفتح الميم وهو مجرى السفينة وسيرها، ومجراها بضم الميم وهو إجراء السفينة وسياقها،

TABATABAI:11:41/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:41/r2.claim: Mursāhā with ḍamma is a verbal noun for mooring, synonymous with establishing or stopping; the author cites 79:32 for the root's sense of setting firm.
TABATABAI:11:41/r2.anchor: المجرى والمرسى مصدرين ميميين وربما احتمل كونه

TABATABAI:11:41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:41/r3.claim: The boarding command is coordinated with the prior arrival of God's command, and Noah addresses his household and other believers or everyone aboard.
TABATABAI:11:41/r3.anchor: وقوله { وقال اركبوا فيها } معطوف على قوله في الآية السابقة { جاء أمرنا } أي حتى إذا قال نوح الخ، وخطابه لأهله وسائر المؤمنين أو لجميع من في السفينة.

TABATABAI:11:41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:41/r4.claim: Noah invokes God's name to bring good and blessing to the ship's sailing and mooring; connecting an act to God's name protects it from ruin, corruption, error, and loss.
TABATABAI:11:41/r4.anchor: تسمية منه عليه السلام يجلب به الخير والبركة لجري السفينة وإرسائها فإن في تعليق فعل من الأفعال أو أمر من الأمور على اسم الله تعالى وربطه به صيانة له من الهلاك والفساد

TABATABAI:11:41/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:41/r5.claim: Sailing and mooring are the visible means of rescue, but they succeed only through God's care for the passengers, including forgiveness and mercy that let them survive and live on earth.
TABATABAI:11:41/r5.anchor: وهذان هما السببان الظاهران في نجاة السفينة ومن فيها من الغرق، وإنما ينجح هذان السببان لو شملت العناية الإلهية من ركبها،

TABATABAI:11:41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:41/r6.claim: Noah explains his invocation by God's forgiveness and mercy: God can preserve the ship's course and mooring from disruption and save them from drowning.
TABATABAI:11:41/r6.anchor: أي إنما أذكر اسم الله على مجرى سفينتي ومرساها لأنه ربي الغفور الرحيم، له أن يحفظ مجراها ومرساها من الاختلال والتخبط حتى ننجو بذلك من الغرق بمغفرته ورحمته.

TABATABAI:11:41/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:41/r7.claim: Noah is the first person whom God reports invoking His noble name in revealed scripture, and the first to establish proof of divine unity, bring scripture and law, and undertake social reform.
TABATABAI:11:41/r7.anchor: ونوح عليه السلام أول إنسان حكى الله سبحانه عنه التسمية باسمه الكريم فيما أوحاه من كتابه فهو عليه السلام أول فاتح فتح هذا الباب كما أنه أول من أقام الحجة على التوحيد،

TABATABAI:11:41/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:41/r8.claim: The preferred reading takes the phrase as Noah's own invocation and majrāhā/mursāhā as verbal nouns; alternatives make it the companions' invocation by his order or treat the nouns as time or place.
TABATABAI:11:41/r8.anchor: وما قدمناه من معنى قوله { بسم الله مجراها ومرساها } مبني على ما هو الظاهر من كون الجملة تسمية من نوح عليه السلام والمجرى والمرسى مصدرين ميميين

TABATABAI:11:41/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r9.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:11:41/r9.claim: Al-Kashshāf allows one sentence with the invocation as a circumstantial phrase at boarding and sailing or mooring, including time or verbal-noun readings with an omitted “time.”
TABATABAI:11:41/r9.anchor: قال في الكشاف في الآية يجوز أن يكون كلاما واحدا وكلامين فالكلام الواحد أن يتصل باسم الله باركبوا حالا من الواو بمعنى اركبوا فيها مسمين الله

TABATABAI:11:41/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:41/r10.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:11:41/r10.claim: Al-Kashshāf also allows majrāhā and mursāhā to mean the places of sailing and mooring, governed by the verbal sense in the invocation.
TABATABAI:11:41/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد مكانا الإجراء والإرساء، وانتصابهما بما في بسم الله من معنى الفعل أو بما فيه من إرادة القول.

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r6.claim: By God's name means that the ship runs through God and settles through Him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r6.anchor: أي بالله تجري، وبه تستقر. ومعنى قلنا باسم الله أي بالله

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r7.claim: Readings include majrāhā with open mīm and marsāhā with ḍamma, both with ḍamma, and other forms; all are correct and good.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r7.anchor: قرئت مجراها بفتح الميم، ومرساها بضم الميم. وقرئت مجراها ومرساها بضم الميمين جميعا

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r8.claim: With open mīm, majrāhā means its running and marsāhā its mooring: by God it is brought to rest.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r8.anchor: فأما من قرأ مجراها بفتح الميم، فالمعنى جريها ومرساها

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r9.claim: With both mīms in ḍamma, the phrase means that God causes it to run and to moor; ajraytuhu and ijrāʾ are synonymous.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r9.anchor: ومن قرأ مجراها ومرساها. فمعنى ذلك بالله إجراؤها وبالله إرساؤها

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r10.claim: The forms may also be understood as the verbal nouns from jarat tajrī and rasat tarsū; al-marsā is its place of rest.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r10.anchor: ومن قال مجراها ومرساها، فهو على جرت جريا ومجرى

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r11.claim: The command is to invoke God's name when the ship is sailing and when it settles; marsāhā is in the genitive as an attribute of God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r11.anchor: والمعنى أن الله جل وعز أمرهم أن يسموا في وقت جريها ووقت استقرارها

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r12.claim: The unrecited form mujrihā should not be read because recitation is transmitted practice, though it admits a circumstantial parse meaning one who runs and moors it.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r12.anchor: ويجوز فيه شيء لم يقرأ به ولا ينبغي أن يقرأ به لأن القراءة سنة متبعة

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r13.claim: On that unrecited form, mujrihā may be an accusative of praise.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على المدح، أعني مجريها ومرسيها

ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r14.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r14.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r14.claim: Alternatively, mujrihā and mursīhā may be nominative with an omitted huwa.
ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مجريها ومرسيها في موضع رفع على إضمار هو مجريها ومرسيها

TABRISI:11:40-42/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:40-42/r2.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
TABRISI:11:40-42/r2.claim: The Kūfan readers except Abū Bakr read majrāhā with fatḥa on the mīm; the others use ḍamma.
TABRISI:11:40-42/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر مجريها بفتح الميم والباقون بضم الميم

TABRISI:11:40-42/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:40-42/r3.speaker: ابن محيصن
TABRISI:11:40-42/r3.claim: All agree on ḍamma in mursal, apart from an anomalous report from Ibn Muḥayṣin opening the mīm in both words.
TABRISI:11:40-42/r3.anchor: واتفقوا على ضم الميم في مرسيها إلا ما يرى في الشواذ عن ابن محيصن أنه فتح الميم فيهما

TABRISI:11:41/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:41/r1.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:41/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī says bismi Allāh majrāhā can be a circumstantial phrase attached either to the pronoun in ride or to the pronoun in it, depending on the syntax.
TABRISI:11:41/r1.anchor: في قوله: { بسم الله مجراها ومرساها } أن يكون حالا من شيئين

TABRISI:11:41/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:41/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:41/r2.claim: If bismi Allāh is a fronted predicate or majrāhā is raised by the adverb, the phrase can only describe the pronoun in it, since it has no reference back to the pronoun in ride.
TABRISI:11:41/r2.anchor: لم يكن { بسم الله مجراها } إلا جملة في موضع الحال

TABRISI:11:41/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:41/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:41/r3.claim: Under another parse, bismi Allāh describes those commanded to ride, as in riding equipped with weapons or clothed; they ride invoking and relying on God.
TABRISI:11:41/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بسم الله حالا من الضمير الذي في قوله { اركبوا }

TABRISI:11:41/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:41/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:41/r4.claim: On that parse, majrāhā attaches to the verbal sense of bismi Allāh and marks the times of running and anchoring; it does not modify ride, since they are not told to board at those times.
TABRISI:11:41/r4.anchor: وجاز تعلقه به لأن يكون ظرفا على نحو مقدم الحاج وخفوق النجم

TABRISI:11:41/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:41/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:11:41/r5.claim: Majrāhā is accusative as an adverb in the latter analysis, and nominative through an initial subject or adverb in the first.
TABRISI:11:41/r5.anchor: فموضع مجريها نصب على هذا الوجه بأنه ظرف عمل فيه المعنى وفي الوجه الأول رفع بالابتداء أو بالظرف

THALABI:v5p170#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p170#2/r1.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي، عبد الله
THALABI:v5p170#2/r1.claim: Abu Raja al-Attaridi, in a reading also attributed to Abdullah, vocalizes both mim letters with damma and the following ra and sin with kasra.
THALABI:v5p170#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو رجاء العطاردي: مجراها ومرساها بضم الميمين وكسر الراء والسين وهي قراءة عبد الله

THALABI:v5p170#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p170#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p170#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the terms mean the ship's place of running and place of mooring, where it comes to rest in the water.
THALABI:v5p170#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: مجراها حيث تجري ومرساها حيث ترسو، أي تحسر في الماء

THALABI:v5p170#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p170#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن محيصن
THALABI:v5p170#2/r3.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads both words with fatḥa as verbal nouns, meaning that God controls the ship's running and settling; the author illustrates the noun pattern with ordinary verbs and a line by Imruʾ al-Qays.
THALABI:v5p170#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن محيصن بفتح الميمين وهما مصدران، يعني أن الله تعالى بيده جريها ورسوها

THALABI:v5p170#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p170#2/r4.speaker: الباقون، أبو عبيد، أبو حاتم
THALABI:v5p170#2/r4.claim: The remaining readers use damma on both mims; Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer this reading, which means God's causing the ship to run and moor, like the cited verbal nouns.
THALABI:v5p170#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم الميمين، واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم، ومعناه: بسم الله إجراؤها وإرساؤها

THALABI:v5p170#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p170#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p170#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says Noah would say Bismillah before mooring the ship and it moored, and say it before setting off and it sailed.
THALABI:v5p170#2/r5.anchor: إن ربي لغفور رحيم قال الضحاك: كان نوح إذا أراد أن يرسو قال: بسم الله، فرست

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r1.claim: Noah tells those he ordered to board to ride; rakiba broadly means to mount or rise onto something, including an animal, ship, land, or sea, and also occurs in the expression for debt burdening someone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r1.anchor: الركوب العلو على ظهر الشيء، فمنه ركوب الدابة، وركوب السفينة، وركوب البر، وركوب البحر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r2.claim: Arabs call passengers on a ship rukāb al-safīna, whereas rukbān, arkūb, and rukb refer to riders of animals and camels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r2.anchor: وتسمي العرب من يركب السفينة ركاب السفينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r3.speaker: ابن أحمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r3.claim: Ibn Aḥmar calls ship passengers rukbānan in a poem, supporting the broader usage for seafarers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r3.anchor: وقد جعل ابن أحمر ركاب السفينة ركبانا فقال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r4.claim: Fī cannot depend on the verb rukūb because Arabic says “I rode the ship,” not “I rode in the ship”; the object is omitted, understood as water, and fīhā is circumstantial.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r4.anchor: لا يجوز أن تكون (في) من صلة الركوب؛ لأنه يقال: ركبت السفينة، ولا يقال: ركبت في السفينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r5.claim: Alternatively, the meaning is “board it,” with fī as an emphatic addition; it directs them to the ark’s interior, since simply saying “board it” might suggest its deck.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال المعنى: اركبوها أي الفلك، وزاد (في) للتأكيد كقوله: {للرؤيا تعبرون} [يوسف: 43]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r1.claim: Majrā is a verbal noun like ijrāʾ; compare “a blessed landing” and the verbal nouns madkhal and makhraj at 17:80.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r1.anchor: المجرى: مصدر كالإجراء، ومثله قوله: {منزلا مباركا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r2.speaker: صاحب هذه القراءة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r2.claim: The reading majrāhā with an open mīm is also a verbal noun like jary; its advocate cites the ship’s running with them in waves in 11:42.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r2.anchor: وقرئ {مجراها} (¬3) بفتح الميم وهو أيضا مصدر مثل الجري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r3.claim: Marsā is a verbal noun from arsā, to become fixed or to make something fixed; 79:32 says God fixed the mountains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r3.anchor: وأما المرسى: فهو أيضا مصدر كالإرساء يقال: وما الشيء يرسو: إذا ثبت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r4.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, says the ship runs by God’s name and power.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5) في رواية عطاء: يريد تجرى باسم الله وقدرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r5.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Noah said “In God’s name” when he wanted the ship to sail, and again when he wanted it to settle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬6): كان إذا أراد أن تجري قال: باسم الله فجرت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the ship sails by God and settles by Him; bismillāh here means “by God,” so the reported explanations share one meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬2): أي بالله تجري وبه تستقر، ومعنى قولنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ offers two parses: majrāhā and marsāhā may be raised by the preposition bi, or bismillāh can stand alone while both nouns are accusative as adverbials of running and settling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r7.anchor: فقال الفراء (¬3): إن شئت جعلت (مجراها) و (مرساها) في موضع رفع بالباء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains the first parse: bi is grammatically the predicate and raises the subject, while its sense is accusative, “its running occurs by God’s name.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r8.anchor: أحدهما: أن يرتفع المجرى بالباء الزائدة، وتفتقر الباء إلى المجرى؛ لأنها خبره ورافعته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r1.speaker: الفراء، ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r1.claim: The second of al-Farrāʾ and Ibn al-Anbārī’s parses makes majrāhā accusative as a time or place expression: “in its running and settling,” with the preposition omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r1.anchor: القول الثاني: أن يكون المجرى في موضع نصب على مذهب الوقت # ومنهاج المحل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r2.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r2.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā supplies an omitted verb for bi; it governs majrāhā, as in “its running and settling take place by God’s name.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r2.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى: الباء منصوبة بفعل محذوف يدل عليه ويكنى (¬2) منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī reads bismillāh as a circumstantial phrase for the riders, who board blessed by God’s name; compare the expression at 5:61.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي (¬3): قوله تعالى: {بسم الله} يجوز أن يكون حالا من الضمير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r4.claim: On his reading, majrāhā and marsāhā are temporal adverbials for the two inevitable periods of sailing and mooring, not times when they are commanded to board.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r4.anchor: ولا يكون الظرف متعلقا باركبوا؛ لأن المعنى ليس (¬4) عليه، ألا ترى أنه لا يراد اركبوا فيها في وقت الجري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī’s circumstantial parse is a separate interpretation from the explanations attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r5.anchor: وهذا الوجه الذي ذكره أبو علي وجه آخر في التفسير سوى ما ذكرنا عن ابن عباس والضحاك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God is forgiving toward the people in the ark and merciful to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): يريد غفور لأصحاب السفينة رحيم بهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r2.claim: The mention of forgiveness and mercy coheres with rescue by boarding: those blessings are obtained through obedience just as rescue was obtained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r2.anchor: لأنه لما ذكرت النجاة بالركوب في السفينة، ذكرت النعمة بالمغفرة والرحمة

BURHAN:v1p390/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.speaker: علماء الظاهر
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.claim: The outward scholars explain the omission as abbreviation from frequent use: the alif of ism is dropped only when appended to Allah and preceded by ba according to the majority.
BURHAN:v1p390/r3.anchor: وعلماء الظاهر يقولون للاختصار وكثرة الاستعمال وهو من خصائص الجلالة الشريفة

BURHAN:v4p302/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.claim: في has spatial containment senses: both place and contained thing may be physical or conceptual, or one physical and one abstract; the first is literal and the fourth metaphor is closest to literal.
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.anchor: للظرفية ثم تارة يكون الظرف والمظروف حسيين نحو زيد في الدار

BURHAN:v4p302/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r11.claim: في may serve as an emphatic particle in the command to embark on Noah's ark.

ITQAN:v4p436/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p436/r7.speaker: الحسين بن علي
ITQAN:v4p436/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sunnī reports from al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī that saying 11:41 when embarking protects the Muslim community from drowning; the report also quotes 39:67.
ITQAN:v4p436/r7.anchor: من حديث الحسين بن علي ( أمان لأمتي من الغرق إذا ركبوا أن يقولوا

ITQAN:v3p16/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p16/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p16/r9.claim: The eye is commonly interpreted as sight or perception; some hold that sense to be literal, with metaphor applying only when the word names the bodily organ.
ITQAN:v3p16/r9.anchor: ومن ذلك العين وهي مؤولة بالبصر أو الإدراك بل قال بعضهم إنها حقيقة في ذلك خلافا

ITQAN:v3p16/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p16/r10.speaker: ابن اللبان
ITQAN:v3p16/r10.claim: Ibn al-Labbān reads divine eyes as God's signs: by them He watches believers and they perceive Him; he supports this through the ark, Moses' upbringing, and the patience passage.
ITQAN:v3p16/r10.anchor: وقال ابن اللبان نسبة العين إليه تعالى اسم لآياته المبصرة التي بها سبحانه ينظر للمؤمنين

ITQAN:v2p486/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p486/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p486/r1.claim: The preposition fī has ten listed senses: place or time, accompaniment, cause, superposition, bi, ilā, min, ʿan, comparison, and emphasis; here it emphasizes the command, meaning ride it.

ITQAN:v3p158/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p158/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p158/r2.claim: At the basmala, infer the act being begun—such as ‘I read’ or ‘I eat’; rhetoricians agree, against grammarians who estimate ‘I begin’ or ‘my beginning.’
ITQAN:v3p158/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا أهل البيان قاطبة خلافا لقول النحاة

DAMGHANI:v1p209/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p209/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p209/r2.claim: Riding here means boarding or being aboard a ship; the cited Noah passage parallels other ship-riding verses.
DAMGHANI:v1p209/r2.anchor: الثالث : الركوب الاستواء في السفينة قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r1.claim: Rukūb means mounting or being atop something; rikāb usually means riding animals.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r1.anchor: الركوب : العلو على الشيء ، والركاب : المطايا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris says related rider terms apply only to camels; al-Khalīl also uses rikāb for a ship's equipment.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r2.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : الركب ، والأركوب ، والركبان والراكبون لا يكونون إلا على جمال

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r3.claim: Rukūb can mean riding beasts and ships.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r3.anchor: أحدهما : الركوب على البهائم والسفن . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p624/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p624/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p624/r2.claim: Hud's wording about carrying fits an ark that bears its passengers; in Al-Mu'minun, where no carrying image is given, سلك aptly describes entering the ark first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p624/r2.anchor: في سورة هود ذكر ما دل على الحمل لأن الحمل جاري في السفينة
